summary: Internal engineering/product planning for Q2 roadmap and launch readiness. Primary focus on launch checklist, infra perf benchmarks (latency/cost), incident postmortem follow-ups, and security gating (SOC2/SSO/VPC). Decisions made: proceed with staged rollout, require infra dry-run and benchmark pass, update runbooks and schedule cross-team rehearsal.
transcript: 00:00 Maya Chen: ok folks, thanks for joining, we'll kick off, um this is the q2 roadmap and launch readiness, try to keep to 60 mins, 00:22 Ethan Park: yea sounds good, I've got slides but i'll save, want to jump right into the checklist and the perf asks? 00:35 Priya Singh: quick FYI, we finished postmortem doc but there are two open gaps on the KV cash expiry, spelled K V cash in the notes, 00:50 Liam O'Connor: (laughs) KV cache, yeah i saw that, the root cause was the cache eviction wasn't honoring the session extension in the canary path, 01:05 Carlos Duarte: we should call that out in the runbook item, also security flagged a SSO regression when we tested on staging last week, 01:20 Maya Chen: right and related to that, security wants the SOC 2 evidence bucket updated, and K-M-S key rotation plan attached, 01:35 Ethan Park: about perf, our staging numbers for p50/p95 are roughly matching the bench, p50 around 45 ms for small prompt but p95 spikes to ~980ms with cold KV misses, 01:52 Priya Singh: those numbers are from the 1.2 release, with quantized kernels? or the full fp16 path? the transcrip sorta says quan-tize but that was a mix up, 02:08 Ethan Park: it's on the quantized runtime on A10g equivalent, though we had one host using an older kernel which caused 20% overhead, 02:25 Maya Chen: so action is to run consistent kernel set across staging hosts, Priya can you own? 02:37 Priya Singh: yep i'll own kernel parity and image rebuilds, 02:44 Maya Chen: great, timeline? 02:47 Priya Singh: aim by thursday, 2026-03-26, 02:53 Liam O'Connor: we should add a perf dry run that's the full e2e not synthetic, with traffic lighting that matches expected production mix, 03:09 Carlos Duarte: I'll schedule that and invite security & SRE, 03:14 Maya Chen: also on rollout strategy, product prefers canary then quick ramp to 10% then 50% if green, engineering would prefer staged increase with automated rollback on regression, 03:32 Ethan Park: agreed on auto rollback, we can leverage the smart routing policy to fallback to hosted variant if dedicated hits errors, though earlier note, fallback compatibility needs model variant compatibility check, 03:53 Priya Singh: we had one mismatch last week where model variant label was slightly different so fallback failed, transcription had 'varient' spelled, 04:07 Maya Chen: ok add compatibility checks into the deployment job, 04:14 Ethan Park: will add an integration test that validates fallback path on canary, 04:20 Maya Chen: security gating, update: SSO issue was due to metadata mismatch from our IDP, looks like the entity-id wasn't updated in the manifest, 04:36 Liam O'Connor: that's fixable, but we need the SOC2 evidence for the customer audit next month, 04:44 Carlos Duarte: Ops will own evidence collection, I'll reach out to compliance to confirm required docs, 05:00 Priya Singh: on incident review follow-ups, the 'prefix cache thrash' item still open, we throttled but didn't root the traffic pattern source, 05:15 Ethan Park: that was caused by a third-party integration churning requests, we'll add rate-limiting and a circuit breaker, 05:28 Maya Chen: what's the priority? 05:31 Priya Singh: high, because it can blow p95 during ramp, 05:35 Liam O'Connor: put it on the incident runbook as P0/P1 so the oncall knows, 05:45 Maya Chen: okay, next security ask is encryption at rest detail for private deployments, customers want confirmation of KMS/HSM support and audit logs, 06:02 Ethan Park: we support cloud KMS and customer-managed keys in the private bundle, H-S-M integration has a couple of manual steps, 06:15 Maya Chen: note that in the doc, but avoid promising full HSM automation until we've scripted it, 06:24 Carlos Duarte: will add a note 'HSM manual steps, planned automation q3', 06:30 Maya Chen: can we confirm data residency controls? some EMEA customers require log partitioning, 06:38 Priya Singh: we can tag logs by region and ship to customer-owned buckets, need to validate retention policy, 06:47 Ethan Park: infra change to log routing will be required but low risk, 06:52 Maya Chen: good. Back to launch checklist items left: bench pass, runbook updated, security docs attached, canary rehearsal scheduled, comms draft, open escalation contacts, rollback plan. 07:12 Priya Singh: on bench pass, need to re-run with consistent kernels and the real prefix caching enabled to measure token cost impact, 07:26 Ethan Park: also include continuous batching changes in the bench matrix, the batching plateau causes different latency profiles, 07:39 Maya Chen: ok include batching knobs and quantization profiles, 07:45 Carlos Duarte: I've got a doc link in the calendar invite, folks, but note the slides had a typo 'quantizaton', 07:53 Maya Chen: (laughs) we've got a lot of typos in this transcript, 08:00 Liam O'Connor: can we set SLOs for the rollout? engineering suggested p95 < 1s and error rate < 0.5% for canary, 08:12 Maya Chen: product ok with those if the cost delta is acceptable, 08:17 Ethan Park: we'll compute cost delta in the bench run and include token level breakdowns, 08:25 Priya Singh: on tooling, we need tracing hooks for per-route latency, the devtools team is working on span tagging but not deployed to staging, 08:39 Ethan Park: i've got a PR open, i'll push to staging after the kernel parity work, 08:47 Maya Chen: perfect. Any risks we haven't covered? 08:50 Priya Singh: infra quota for dedicated GPUs might be tight next week, 08:56 Liam O'Connor: we're provisioning reserve capacity but need approval from finance if we exceed commit, 09:05 Maya Chen: finance signoff timeline? 09:08 Carlos Duarte: we can file request today, but timing might push to next monday, 09:12 Maya Chen: note for launch plan if we need to slow ramp. 09:18 Ethan Park: quick callout about competitor benching, OpenAI has a different batching behavior that yields better throughput for short prompts but worse for long sequences, we should highlight that in customer-facing docs, 09:34 Priya Singh: also mention NVidia optimizations and kernel selection impact, 09:39 Maya Chen: ok include competitor callouts as a short appendix. 09:44 Liam O'Connor: on canary rehearsal, let's do it with the SRE runbook and mimic a regen traffic spike, 09:55 Carlos Duarte: i'll coordinate and send invites, target 2026-03-25 for rehearsal, 10:02 Maya Chen: recap, next steps: Ethan runs perf dry run (due 2026-03-26), Priya updates runbook (due 2026-03-23), Maya sends comms + checklist (due 2026-03-24), Carlos schedules rehearsal (due 2026-03-25). 10:20 Priya Singh: I'll also add the KV cache TTL tests to the bench, 10:29 Ethan Park: noted, will validate fallback variant labels in deployment job. 10:35 Maya Chen: any final Qs? (silence) ok thanks everyone, we'll reconvene after the dry run and finalize launch date, 10:46 Liam O'Connor: thanks, bye, 10:50 (end)
